compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Intel Arc B580 via D3D12 HLSL cs_6_8, fp16 buffers, no HLSL linalg, single dispatch, 32 KiB groupshared cap, wave size should be explicitly 32 if wave-owned mapping is used.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: This is a dense high-arithmetic 3x3 convolution with ReLU and 2x2 average-pool fusion. Main work is approximately 128*180*320*4*128*9 MACs, so compute dominates once memory reuse is reasonable.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Without matrix/linalg intrinsics, scalar/vector FMA throughput and compiler lowering of float16_t or float accumulations are major unknowns.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input tensor is 1x128x360x640 fp16, weights are 128x128x3x3 fp16, bias is 128 fp16, output is 1x128x180x320 fp16. Dense contiguous row-major accesses; naive direct output computation rereads overlapping input and weights heavily. Full fusion avoids materializing the intermediate 1x128x360x640 conv/ReLU tensor.
memory_bandwidth.risk: A no-cache/no-tile mapping may repeatedly stream tens of GB of input/weight traffic and underuse spatial and output-channel reuse.

register_pressure.notes: A fused pooled output needs four independent convolution accumulators because ReLU precedes average pooling. Per-thread variants therefore carry at least 4 accumulators plus loop/index state; output-channel-vector variants multiply this pressure.
register_pressure.risk: Trying to compute too many output channels or spatial cells per thread can reduce occupancy and spill, while overusing groupshared would exceed the 32 KiB D3D limit.

action.description: Implement a fused shader where each worker computes complete pooled outputs for one output channel and one or a small number of spatial positions, keeping the four pre-pool convolution accumulators in registers and streaming input/weights directly from SRVs.
action.rationale: This is the fastest correctness-oriented first implementation: it fuses convolution, ReLU, and average pooling, avoids the large intermediate tensor, requires no groupshared memory or barriers, and gives a reliable baseline for later tiling.

action.description: Implement a fused shader where a threadgroup owns a spatial tile for one or a small number of output channels, accumulates four conv positions per output in registers, and cooperatively stages only reusable input-channel blocks and/or compact weight blocks as read-only groupshared tiles.
action.rationale: This is the highest-upside family because it attacks both major reuse sources: overlapping input neighborhoods across nearby pooled cells and repeated use of the same output-channel weights across many spatial outputs, while still avoiding intermediate global tensors.
action.title: Group-owned spatial/channel tile with selective shared read-only tiles

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Must keep total groupshared below 32 KiB in cs_6_8. Best suited to fixed H/W/C constants and single-dispatch static indexing.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: The mapping exposes many independent output-channel/spatial lanes, uses FP32 accumulators, and keeps the 21.25 KiB groupshared allocation below the 32 KiB DXIL limit. Barriers are the main remaining structural cost.

memory_bandwidth.notes: The current best code behavior matches this family: a compact read-only reusable input tile is cooperatively loaded once per IC block and consumed by 16 output-channel waves across many spatial cells, saving substantial SRV traffic.

register_pressure.notes: Eight accumulators per lane plus tile indexing is moderate. Further unrolling or more pooled outputs per lane may risk occupancy loss, but current pressure appears acceptable on Arc B580.

kernel_summary: The target kernel is a fixed-shape dense fp16 Conv2D(128->128, 3x3, stride1, zero padding) followed by ReLU, identity/non-quantized activation quantizer, and AvgPool2d(2), producing 1x128x180x320. The best high-level approach is full fusion in one HLSL cs_6_8 dispatch: compute each pooled output from the four corresponding conv positions, apply ReLU before averaging, and write fp16 once, avoiding the enormous intermediate conv/ReLU tensor. The workload is compute-heavy but naive streaming still rereads weights and overlapping input heavily; candidate mappings trade simplicity, wave-level reduction parallelism, and threadgroup tile reuse. Groupshared memory should only be used for compact read-only reusable input/weight tiles with explicit producer/consumer reuse and barriers, never for materializing whole phase tensors, and must stay well below the 32 KiB D3D/DXIL limit.
